title: Check yourself: Metrics, evaluation sets and where a headline hides the failure

questions.stem: Two versions of a support assistant both score 92 percent on the evaluation set. One of them gets refund answers wrong far more often, and a wrong refund answer costs twenty times a wrong status answer. What should the report show?

options.text: Accuracy by type of case, with each mistake priced
options.says: A table by segment with the cost of the errors shows the regression that the overall figure averages away.

options.text: The overall accuracy alone, as the two scores are equal
options.says: Ruled out because "Equal overall scores can hide unequal failures".

options.text: The average latency, as users notice speed before all else
options.says: Ruled out because "A figure from another dimension cannot stand in for the segment that is failing".

options.text: The size of the set, as a larger set makes the score fair
options.says: Ruled out because "More cases make the score steadier and do not show where it is low".

origin.section: Where a headline hides the failure

questions.stem: A team grades a research assistant's free-form reports only with exact-match checks, and the score barely moves when the quality of the reports visibly changes. Which addition fits best?

options.text: A longer answer key, so that more phrasings of each answer count as a match
options.says: Ruled out because "Exact match suits answers with one correct form and rejects a correct report that is worded differently".

options.text: Human review of every report, since people are the only judges whose verdict is valid, whatever the cost in time
options.says: Ruled out because "Human review of every output does not scale".

options.text: A rubric-driven model judge, with people sampling its misses
options.says: Free text has no single correct form, so a rubric grader scales and people sample for what it misses.

options.text: Fewer test cases of higher quality, each of them graded by hand with great care
options.says: Ruled out because the documentation advises "More questions with slightly lower signal automated grading is better than fewer questions with high-quality human hand-graded evals".

origin.section: Mixed methods: one grader per kind of output
